Loss-of-function mutations in the APC gene disrupt the negative regulation of the Wnt signaling pathway. This leads to the accumulation of beta-catenin, which then translocates to the nucleus and promotes the transcription of genes involved in cell proliferation and survival. This dysregulated Wnt signaling is a key driver in the development of intestinal polyposis (familial adenomatous polyposis 2) and also contributes significantly to the pathogenesis of gastric cancer.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in APC were found to predominantly cause gain-of-function effects in one of the diseases, or if the Wnt signaling pathway was not demonstrably activated in the tumor microenvironment of both disease types, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: rs112935841)_

#### 2. Tessadori-Van Haaften neurodevelopmental syndrome 4  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.469)

This disruption leads to accumulation of unrepaired DNA damage, which can manifest as increased cancer risk (familial adenomatous polyposis 2) and neurodevelopmental abnormalities (Tessadori-Van Haaften neurodevelopmental syndrome 4) due to compromised DNA replication and repair integrity in critical cellular contexts.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the specific variants in MUTYH associated with Tessadori-Van Haaften neurodevelopmental syndrome 4 do not impair base excision repair or that the downstream consequences on DNA replication and repair integrity are topologically distinct from those leading to FAP2. _(variant: Any common variant (AF > 0.1%) in MUTYH associated with either disease.)_

#### 3. nonpapillary renal cell carcinoma  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.425)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-110330, Reactome:R-HSA-110331, Reactome:R-HSA-110357)
